links.outcome: Effect of human-AI adjudication on reference label quality and agent error
links.effect: Adjudication revised 127 (20%) of 626 initial expert labels and added 60 notes; agent MAE improved from 0.406 to 0.291 against the 686-note co-produced reference.
links.quote: Expert reviewers labeled 626 notes from 273 patients; human-AI adjudication revised 127 (20%) of these initial labels and added 60 newly labeled notes, yielding a 686-note co-produced reference.

links.outcome: Accuracy and cost of budget-tiered configuration versus high-reasoning GPT-5.4 configuration
links.effect: Budget-tiered configuration matched GPT-5.4 high reasoning accuracy while reducing estimated cost by 69% and compute time by 70%.
links.quote: Applied across the cohort, the agent labeled 101,691 notes; the budget tiered configuration matched the accuracy of GPT-5.4 at high reasoning effort while reducing estimated cost by 69% and compute time by 70%.

unlisted_practices: Human-AI co-learning adjudication loop to refine gold-standard labels for EHR phenotyping
Agent-generated ambiguity flags to route notes for focused expert review
Budget-tiered model configuration (cheaper model for extraction, stronger for reasoning) for resource-efficient scaling
